newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end 1.53 pct higher.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end 1.53 pct higher.

text.p: Sustained active buying of heavyweights and medium-caps such as Telkom, Sampoerna and Citra Marga pushed the Jakarta Composite Index to a new 1997 high on Monday, brokers said.

The index closed up 10.16 points on the day, or 1.53 percent, at 674.13 points. Gainers led losers by 78 to 44, with 55 counters unchanged. Total volume was 212.0 million shares on a turnover of 438.9 billion rupiah.

Brokers said the index was at its highest level since April 1990 when it hit a record 681.94 points. "This is really a bullish market, I hope it will continue tomorrow," a broker with a foreign firm said.
"There was a lot of capital inflow to the bourse today, maybe due to the gradually declining interest rate," said another foreign broker.
Brokers said the market was likely to continue making gains on Tuesday with blue-chips like Telkom and Sampoerna leading the upward trend.
Brokers and analysts said the rise was in line with higher Dow Jones close on Friday. Jakarta also received a boost from strong regional markets, excluding Japan which dropped 609.70 points.
"The Nikkei index does not have much effect on the Jakarta bourse. Hong Kong has much more influence," an analyst with a Singapore-based firm said.
Brokers said foreign investors were active from the opening with the focus on Telkom -- with 18.2 percent weight in the index -- Sampoerna and Citra Marga helping boost overall market sentiment.
Telecommunications firm Telkom rose 125 rupiah to 4,125 rupiah on a volume of 3.7 million shares, boosted by its higher closing price of $34-1/8 in New York on Friday.
Cigarette maker Sampoerna rose 750 rupiah to 14,825 rupiah on a volume of 1.9 million shares on what brokers said was its fundamentals.
Toll road operator Citra Marga rose 100 rupiah to 1,975 rupiah with 5.4 million shares changing hands despite a report that its its proposed $100 million notes got a BBB-minus from the S&P.
Standard & Poor's said on Monday it had assigned a BBB-minus rating to the proposed US$100 million 144A notes issue by Citra Marga Finance BV, which is guaranteed by PT Citra Marga Nusphala Persada.
Brokers said in late trade, sentiment on Citra Marga was improved following a report that it had a 1996 net profit of 123.6 billion rupiah.
Bank Negara Indonesia was the most active stock. It rose 50 rupiah to 1,450 rupiah with about 37.4 million shares traded on expectations that its 1996 earnings would be better than forecast.
Medium-sized retailer Matahari Putra Prima and Multipolar Corporation were also actively traded on expectations both companies would have better result from their cooperation.
Brokers said rises in both stocks were linked to Multipolar's plan to take a 50.1 percent stake in Matahari, subject to shareholders' approval at an extraordinary general meeting on January 30.

Multipolar rose 150 rupiah to 2,050 rupiah on a volume of 10.4 million shares, while Matahari rose 225 rupiah to 3,100 rupiah on 6.3 million shares. Brokers said sentiment on Multipolar had also received a boost from market talk of a possible stock split.

Secondary Hero Supermarket also made good gains on speculation that a unit of the Lippo Group would acquire or take over the company, brokers said. Hero rose 225 rupiah to 2,125 rupiah on a volume of 3.2 million shares. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
